📍 Job Overview
Job Title: Digital Workflow Developer — Rapid Prototyping and Pilots for NATO with security clearance
Company: WLG
Location: Bucharest, Romania
Job Type: Full-time
Category: Operations Technology / Workflow Development
Date Posted: 2026-10-06
Experience Level: 2-5 Years
Remote Status: On-site
🚀 Role Summary
Drive rapid prototyping and development of digital workflows and operational pilots, directly supporting NATO's capability development initiatives.
Focus on hands-on software development, transforming user needs into functional, iterative prototypes using approved platforms and AI-assisted tooling.
Collaborate closely with process owners and operational users to understand current workflows and design future-state solutions that enhance efficiency and data integrity.
Ensure all development adheres to strict security, data management, and licensing constraints within NATO-approved environments.
📝 Enhancement Note: This role is highly specialized, focusing on the practical, hands-on development of digital workflows and prototypes for a critical defense organization. The emphasis is on tangible delivery and iterative improvement based on user feedback, rather than high-level strategy or project management. The requirement for direct, personal development experience is paramount.
📈 Primary Responsibilities
Conduct rapid, hands-on development of digital workflow prototypes and operational pilots on approved NATO platforms.
Engage directly with process owners and operational users to meticulously document current workflows, identifying roles, states, decision points, and data exchanges.
Translate complex operational needs into minimum viable prototypes (MVPs) that can be swiftly built, demonstrated, and refined.
Design and configure structured data capture mechanisms, define roles, establish business rules, implement validation checks, and manage routing and approval processes.
Develop and implement status tracking features for workflows, ensuring visibility and control.
Integrate prototypes with approved data sources via interfaces, databases, web services, or structured file exchanges.
Write lightweight scripts or develop custom components when configurable tooling alone is insufficient to prove a concept.
Utilize approved AI-assisted development tooling strategically to accelerate prototyping efforts.
Execute user testing and operational pilots, iterating on the prototype based on observed user behavior and feedback rather than initial assumptions.
Measure and document the impact of developed solutions against established baselines, focusing on metrics such as cycle time, manual effort reduction, and data completeness.
Proactively identify and address security, data management, licensing, hosting, and sustainment constraints throughout the development lifecycle.
📝 Enhancement Note: The primary focus of this role is on the "build" aspect of development. Responsibilities emphasize direct coding, configuration, and iterative refinement of software prototypes, with a strong emphasis on user-centric design and tangible results. The iterative nature and the need to measure impact are key operational components.
🎓 Skills & Qualifications
Education:
University degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Software Engineering, Human-Centered Design, Business Process Management, or a closely related field.
Equivalent practical experience will be considered in lieu of a formal degree.
Experience:
A minimum of twelve months of hands-on development experience within the last twenty-four months, focusing on building digital applications, workflows, or prototypes.
At least two of the last five years must be dedicated to low-code, no-code, or configurable application development platforms outside of the Microsoft ecosystem.
Demonstrated experience building at least two distinct solutions using low-code/no-code platforms, with at least one solution having been deployed and used by real end-users.
Hands-on development experience across at least two different rapid-development platforms.
Experience in directing, supervising, advising, or product ownership does not fulfill the hands-on build requirement.
Required Skills:
Rapid Prototyping: Proven ability to quickly build functional proof-of-concept applications and workflows.
Digital Workflow Development: Expertise in designing, configuring, and implementing end-to-end digital workflows.
Low-Code/No-Code Platforms: Deep practical experience with at least two distinct platforms (non-Microsoft) for application and workflow development.
Software Engineering Fundamentals: Solid understanding of software development principles, even within low-code/no-code environments.
Business Process Management (BPM): Ability to analyze, document, and optimize business processes.
User Testing & Feedback Integration: Skill in conducting user tests and iteratively improving solutions based on feedback.
Data Capture & Management: Experience in designing and configuring structured data capture, validation, and routing rules.
System Integration: Capability to connect prototypes with external data sources via APIs, databases, or file exchanges.
Scripting/Lightweight Development: Ability to write basic scripts or develop small components for enhanced functionality.
AI-Assisted Development Tooling: Familiarity and proficiency in using AI tools to accelerate development.
Requirement Analysis: Strong ability to elicit and document detailed functional and non-functional requirements from stakeholders.
Technical Documentation: Proficiency in documenting workflows, system configurations, and technical specifications.
Fluent Professional English: Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Preferred Skills:
Experience with specific NATO-approved rapid development platforms.
Familiarity with defense sector operational environments and security protocols.
Human-centered design principles applied to workflow development.
Experience with AI-assisted development tools beyond basic usage.
📝 Enhancement Note: The qualifications heavily emphasize practical, hands-on building experience, particularly outside the Microsoft stack. The distinction between "building" and "directing/managing" is critical. This indicates a need for developers who can translate concepts into tangible, working software independently.
📊 Process & Systems Portfolio Requirements
Portfolio Essentials:
Demonstrated Workflow Prototypes: Showcase at least two distinct digital workflow prototypes or MVPs developed on non-Microsoft low-code/no-code platforms, highlighting their functionality and user interaction.
Process Optimization Case Studies: Include detailed case studies of at least one project where you analyzed a current workflow, designed an improved digital version, and demonstrated its impact (e.g., reduced cycle time, improved data accuracy).
System Integration Examples: Provide evidence of integrating prototypes with external data sources, such as database connections, API calls, or structured file imports/exports.
User-Centric Design Evidence: Illustrate how user feedback was incorporated into the iterative development process of a prototype, showing before-and-after improvements.
Process Documentation:
Workflow Mapping: Present examples of current and future-state workflow diagrams, detailing roles, states, decision points, and data exchanges.
Configuration Documentation: Provide samples of how you documented configurations for data capture, business rules, routing logic, and approval processes within a rapid development platform.
Performance Measurement Artifacts: Include examples of how you measured and reported on the performance of a prototype or pilot, such as baseline metrics vs. post-implementation results (e.g., cycle time reduction charts, data completeness reports).
📝 Enhancement Note: A strong portfolio demonstrating hands-on building and iterative development is crucial. Candidates should be prepared to walk through their prototypes, explain their design choices, and articulate the measurable impact of their work, especially concerning process efficiency and data integrity.
💵 Compensation & Benefits
Salary Range:
Given the specialized nature of the role, the requirement for security clearance, relocation assistance, and the long-term engagement for NATO, a competitive salary is expected. For a developer with 2-5 years of relevant hands-on experience in Bucharest, Romania, typical full-time salaries for similar technical roles can range from €25,000 to €45,000 annually, depending on the specific platform expertise and the depth of experience. However, due to the unique client (NATO) and relocation package, the actual salary could be higher and will be determined by WLG's delivery partner based on candidate qualifications and the specific contract terms.
Benefits:
Visa Sponsorship: NATO-5 visa sponsorship provided for the candidate and their family, facilitating relocation to the United States.
Relocation Assistance: Comprehensive support for relocating to Norfolk, Virginia, USA.
Full Employment Contract: Direct employment with WLG's delivery partner, offering stability and standard employment benefits, not a contractor arrangement.
Long-Term Engagement: This is a long-term, renewable engagement, providing job security and consistent work.
Professional Development: Opportunities to work on critical defense projects and potentially gain experience with advanced technologies and secure environments.
Health and Welfare Benefits: Standard benefits provided by the delivery partner (details to be confirmed).
Working Hours:
Typically 40 hours per week, consistent with full-time employment. Flexibility may be available, but the on-site requirement in Norfolk, Virginia, will be primary.
📝 Enhancement Note: The salary estimate is based on local market rates for Bucharest for similar technical roles, adjusted upwards due to the specialized nature, security clearance, and comprehensive relocation package. The benefits, particularly visa sponsorship and relocation, are significant value-adds for candidates looking to transition internationally.
🎯 Team & Company Context
🏢 Company Culture
Industry: Technology Services / Government & Defense Contracting. WLG operates as a technology consulting and delivery partner, specializing in complex projects, often for government or large enterprise clients. Their focus is on delivering tangible solutions through skilled technical teams.
Company Size: WLG is part of a larger entity, but the specific delivery partner employing the candidate will likely be a focused team of developers and project managers. The description implies a structure designed to support large, long-term engagements like the NATO project.
Founded: Information not directly provided, but WLG's presence suggests an established firm with experience in government and defense sectors.
Team Structure:
The operations technology team is likely structured to support specific client projects, such as this NATO engagement. It will comprise developers, potentially business analysts, and project managers, all focused on delivering software solutions.
Reporting will be through a delivery partner's management structure, with direct collaboration with NATO process owners and operational users on-site.
Cross-functional collaboration will be essential, involving close interaction with NATO personnel to understand requirements and with internal team members for technical support and knowledge sharing.
Methodology:
Data-Driven Development: Emphasis on measuring performance against baselines and iterating based on observed data and user feedback.
Agile/Iterative Prototyping: Rapid development cycles focused on delivering working software quickly and refining it through continuous feedback.
User-Centric Design: Prioritizing the needs and experiences of the end-users in the design and development process.
Secure Development Practices: Adherence to strict security protocols and guidelines relevant to defense organizations.
Company Website: https://career.wlgroup.eu
📝 Enhancement Note: The company culture is geared towards delivering complex, long-term technical solutions for critical clients. Expect a professional, results-oriented environment with a strong emphasis on technical delivery, process adherence, and client satisfaction, particularly within a secure, defense-oriented context.
📈 Career & Growth Analysis
Operations Career Level: This role is positioned as a hands-on developer, focusing on execution rather than strategic oversight. It's ideal for an individual contributor who excels at building and iterating software solutions. The "Digital Workflow Developer" title suggests a specialization within software engineering, focused on process automation and application development.
Reporting Structure: The developer will report to a manager within WLG's delivery partner organization. However, a significant portion of their time will be spent working directly with NATO process owners and end-users on-site, requiring strong self-management and direct communication skills.
Operations Impact: The developer's work directly impacts NATO's capability development by digitizing processes and proving the value of new software solutions through working prototypes and pilots. This accelerates decision-making and implementation of improved operational capabilities, leading to increased efficiency, better data management, and enhanced operational effectiveness.
Growth Opportunities:
Specialization: Deepen expertise in specific low-code/no-code platforms and workflow automation technologies, becoming a subject matter expert.
Client-Side Expertise: Develop extensive experience working within defense organizations and understanding their unique operational challenges and security requirements.
Leadership Potential: With proven success, opportunities may arise to lead small teams of developers on future projects, mentor junior developers, or take on more complex architectural responsibilities within prototypes.
Broader Skill Development: Opportunity to gain experience with AI-assisted development tools and potentially other integration technologies as projects evolve.
📝 Enhancement Note: This role offers a clear path for hands-on technical growth within a specialized domain (defense workflow automation). Career progression is likely tied to deepening technical skills, successfully delivering complex projects, and demonstrating leadership potential within the delivery partner's structure.
🌐 Work Environment
Office Type: The role requires relocation to Norfolk, Virginia, USA, and will be performed on-site. This implies working within a professional office environment, likely within facilities or offices designated for NATO-related projects or WLG's delivery partner.
Office Location(s): Norfolk, Virginia, USA. This location is significant as it's a major hub for naval operations and NATO activities in the United States.
Workspace Context:
Collaborative Environment: Expect a dynamic workspace that fosters close collaboration with NATO process owners, operational users, and fellow developers. This will involve frequent direct interaction, feedback sessions, and co-creation.
Technology Access: Access to approved development platforms, AI-assisted tooling, and necessary IT infrastructure to build and test prototypes. Security protocols will dictate the exact technology stack and access levels.
On-Site Interaction: The role is fundamentally on-site, necessitating direct engagement with the user base to understand their workflows and gather immediate feedback for iterative development.
Work Schedule: Standard full-time work schedule (approximately 40 hours per week) is expected, with the primary requirement being on-site presence in Norfolk, Virginia. While some flexibility in daily hours might be possible, the focus is on consistent availability for client and team collaboration.
📝 Enhancement Note: The on-site requirement in Norfolk, Virginia, is a critical aspect of this role, emphasizing direct collaboration and immersion in the client's operational environment. Candidates should be prepared for a structured work setting within a defense-related context.
📄 Application & Portfolio Review Process
Interview Process:
Initial Screening: A review of your CV and portfolio to assess hands-on development experience, specific platform expertise (non-Microsoft low-code/no-code), and alignment with rapid prototyping requirements.
Technical Interview: This will likely involve in-depth discussions about your past projects, focusing on your direct contributions to building digital workflows and prototypes. Be prepared to explain your approach to understanding user needs, designing solutions, configuring platforms, and integrating systems.
Portfolio Presentation/Walkthrough: You may be asked to present one or more key projects from your portfolio, demonstrating the functionality of prototypes, explaining your development process, and quantifying the impact or improvements achieved.
Scenario-Based/Problem-Solving: You might be given a hypothetical workflow challenge and asked to outline how you would approach prototyping a solution, including the platforms you'd consider and the steps you'd take.
Cultural Fit & Relocation Discussion: Interviews will also assess your ability to work collaboratively with diverse teams (NATO and WLG), your understanding of working in a secure environment, and your readiness for relocation to Norfolk, Virginia.
Portfolio Review Tips:
Highlight Hands-On Contribution: Clearly articulate your direct role in building each project. Use "I" statements and focus on your technical contributions.
Showcase Non-Microsoft Platforms: Emphasize your experience with low-code/no-code platforms other than Microsoft products.
Demonstrate Iteration: Show how you used user feedback or testing results to refine and improve prototypes.
Quantify Impact: Whenever possible, use metrics (e.g., "reduced cycle time by X%", "improved data accuracy to Y%", "handled Z transactions") to illustrate the value of your work.
Visuals are Key: Include screenshots, short video demos, or clear diagrams of your prototypes to make your work tangible.
Focus on Workflow Design: Clearly explain the business problem, the workflow you designed, and the specific features you implemented to solve it.
Challenge Preparation:
Workflow Analysis: Practice analyzing simple business processes and sketching out potential digital workflow solutions.
Platform Familiarity: Refresh your knowledge of the rapid development platforms you've used, focusing on their configuration capabilities for data, rules, and routing.
User Story Formulation: Practice writing user stories from the perspective of operational users to capture requirements effectively.
📝 Enhancement Note: The interview process is heavily weighted towards practical demonstration of building skills. Candidates must be ready to prove their hands-on experience with specific platforms and articulate the impact of their development work.
🛠 Tools & Technology Stack
Primary Tools:
Rapid Development Platforms (Low-Code/No-Code): Extensive hands-on experience with at least two distinct platforms outside the Microsoft ecosystem (e.g., Mendix, OutSystems, Appian, Pega, ServiceNow App Engine, or similar). The ability to quickly learn and adapt to NATO-approved platforms will be critical.
AI-Assisted Development Tooling: Familiarity and proficiency with AI tools that enhance prototyping speed and code generation. Specific tools will be dictated by NATO approval.
Scripting Languages: Lightweight scripting capabilities (e.g., JavaScript, Python, shell scripting) for custom components or integrations.
Analytics & Reporting:
Built-in Platform Analytics: Proficiency in utilizing the reporting and analytics features inherent to the low-code/no-code platforms used.
Data Visualization Tools: Ability to create dashboards and reports to present performance metrics (e.g., cycle time, error rates, user adoption) to stakeholders, potentially using tools integrated within the platforms or standard BI tools if approved.
CRM & Automation:
While not explicitly a CRM role, understanding how workflows interact with data sources and potentially CRM systems is beneficial.
Workflow Automation Tools: Deep understanding of configuring and implementing automated business processes, including triggers, actions, approvals, and notifications.
Integration Tools: Experience with integrating applications via APIs, web services, or structured file exchange mechanisms.
📝 Enhancement Note: Proficiency in non-Microsoft low-code/no-code platforms is a non-negotiable requirement. Candidates should be prepared to discuss their experience with specific platforms and demonstrate how they've leveraged them for rapid prototyping and workflow automation.
👥 Team Culture & Values
Operations Values:
Delivery Excellence: A strong commitment to delivering high-quality, functional software prototypes and pilots that meet client requirements and exceed expectations.
User Focus: Prioritizing the needs and experiences of the end-users, ensuring that developed solutions are practical, intuitive, and solve real problems.
Adaptability & Agility: Embracing iterative development, being responsive to feedback, and quickly adapting to changing requirements or new insights gained during prototyping.
Integrity & Security: Upholding the highest standards of data security, confidentiality, and ethical conduct, especially within a defense context.
Collaboration: Fostering a team environment where open communication, knowledge sharing, and mutual support are paramount, both within the WLG team and with NATO stakeholders.
Collaboration Style:
Direct & Frequent Communication: Expect a collaborative style characterized by regular, direct communication with process owners and users to ensure alignment and gather feedback.
Hands-On Partnership: Working closely with stakeholders in a co-creation manner, demonstrating prototypes and incorporating feedback in real-time or near real-time.
Cross-Functional Teamwork: Collaborating effectively with other developers, project managers, and potentially security or IT personnel within WLG's delivery partner structure.
Feedback-Oriented: A culture that encourages constructive feedback, both giving and receiving, to drive continuous improvement in both the product and the development process.
📝 Enhancement Note: The emphasis on user focus, collaboration, and adaptability is key. Candidates should demonstrate an understanding of working closely with clients in a hands-on, iterative manner, particularly within the structured environment of defense contracting.
⚡ Challenges & Growth Opportunities
Challenges:
Security & Compliance: Navigating and adhering to stringent NATO security protocols, data handling policies, and approval processes for development tools and environments.
Platform Constraints & Integration: Working within approved platforms and integrating with potentially legacy or complex NATO data systems, which may require creative problem-solving.
Rapid Iteration Demands: The need to deliver functional prototypes quickly and iterate based on feedback can be demanding, requiring efficient development practices and clear communication.
Cross-Cultural Collaboration: Effectively communicating and collaborating with NATO personnel from various backgrounds and with diverse operational perspectives.
Relocation Logistics: Managing the complexities of international relocation for oneself and family to a new country and a new role.
Learning & Development Opportunities:
Specialized Platform Expertise: Gaining deep expertise in specific, enterprise-grade low-code/no-code platforms commonly used in large organizations and government sectors.
Defense Sector Domain Knowledge: Developing a strong understanding of NATO operations, defense capabilities, and the unique challenges faced by military organizations.
Advanced Prototyping Techniques: Honing skills in rapid prototyping, user-centered design, and iterative development within complex environments.
AI-Assisted Development: Becoming proficient in leveraging AI tools to accelerate software development workflows.
International Project Experience: Building a career portfolio with high-impact international defense projects.
📝 Enhancement Note: Candidates should be prepared to discuss how they approach challenges related to security, integration, and rapid iteration. Highlighting adaptability and a proactive learning mindset will be crucial for success.

📍 Job Overview
Job Title: Senior UX Engineer
Company: Lenovo
Location: Bucharest, Romania
Job Type: Full-time
Category: User Experience (UX) Design / Engineering
Date Posted: October 2, 2026
Experience Level: Mid-Senior Level (5-10 years)
Remote Status: Hybrid
🚀 Role Summary
Lead the end-to-end user experience (UX) vision for Lenovo's Hybrid Cloud and Agentic AI platform portfolio, ensuring a cohesive and intuitive user journey across all modules.
Drive UX strategy and experience differentiation for complex, multi-domain enterprise workflows, focusing on user-centered design principles and scalable solutions.
Design seamless cross-module user journeys that integrate AIOps, FinOps, TokenOps, AI Computing, Cloud Native, Security, and Governance functionalities.
Establish and maintain UX principles, standards, and interaction patterns, fostering consistency and best practices across the entire platform.
Collaborate closely with global Product Management and Engineering teams to translate enterprise customer needs into innovative and technically feasible UX solutions.
📝 Enhancement Note: This role is positioned as a Senior UX Engineer, indicating a focus on both strategic UX vision and hands-on design execution. The emphasis on "Hybrid Cloud and Agentic AI platform portfolio" suggests a deep dive into complex enterprise software solutions, requiring a strong understanding of modern cloud architectures and AI-driven functionalities. The hybrid work arrangement implies a need for strong self-management and communication skills.
📈 Primary Responsibilities
Define and own the overarching UX vision for Lenovo’s Hybrid Cloud and Agentic AI platform, ensuring seamless integration and user flow across all product modules.
Lead UX strategy development and execution for intricate, multi-domain enterprise workflows, focusing on innovative experience differentiation.
Design and prototype user journeys that span critical areas such as AIOps, FinOps, TokenOps, AI Computing, Cloud Native, Security, and Governance.
Establish and champion UX principles, interaction patterns, and design standards to ensure a consistent and high-quality user experience across the platform.
Partner effectively with Product Managers to deeply understand enterprise customer needs and translate them into scalable, user-centric UX solutions.
Collaborate closely with Engineering teams to ensure UX decisions are aligned with platform architecture, technical constraints, and development timelines.
Drive the evolution, adoption, and maintenance of a scalable design system that supports multiple product surfaces and enhances design efficiency.
Act as a vocal advocate for user-centered design practices, influencing product, engineering, and go-to-market teams to prioritize user needs.
📝 Enhancement Note: The responsibilities highlight a blend of strategic leadership and hands-on design. The explicit mention of AIOps, FinOps, and TokenOps suggests a need for domain-specific understanding within the cloud and AI operations space. The focus on "design systems" implies a need for systematic thinking and component-based design approaches.
🎓 Skills & Qualifications
Education: Bachelor’s degree in Design, Human-Computer Interaction (HCI), Computer Science, or a closely related field, or equivalent practical experience demonstrating a strong foundation in design principles and user-centered methodologies.
Experience: Minimum of 6 years of dedicated UX or product design experience, with at least 3 of those years focused on enterprise software, Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) platforms, or complex cloud-based environments.
Required Skills:
UX Strategy & Vision: Proven ability to define and articulate a comprehensive UX vision for complex product portfolios, aligning with business objectives.
Enterprise-Level Design: Demonstrated experience in designing for complex, multi-module enterprise systems, ensuring cross-surface consistency and scalability.
User Journey Mapping: Expertise in mapping and designing intricate user journeys across various functional domains within a platform.
Interaction Design & IA: Strong proficiency in interaction design principles and information architecture to create intuitive and efficient user flows.
Design Tools Proficiency: Hands-on experience with modern design and prototyping tools, specifically Figma and FigJam, for creating wireframes, mockups, and interactive prototypes.
Design Systems: Experience in building, scaling, and maintaining design systems in collaboration with cross-functional teams to ensure design consistency and efficiency.
User Research & Advocacy: Ability to advocate for and apply user-centered design practices, informed by user research insights.
Communication & Collaboration: Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with a strong ability to collaborate effectively with global, cross-functional teams and stakeholders.
English Proficiency: Professional working proficiency in English (spoken and written) for effective global communication.
Preferred Skills:
Hybrid Cloud & AI Platform Knowledge: Familiarity with concepts and user needs within Hybrid Cloud, Agentic AI, AIOps, FinOps, or TokenOps.
SaaS & Cloud Platform Experience: Deep understanding of user experience challenges and best practices within SaaS and cloud platform environments.
Prototyping & User Testing: Experience in creating high-fidelity prototypes and conducting user testing to validate design solutions.
Agile Methodologies: Familiarity with Agile development processes and how UX integrates into iterative development cycles.
Stakeholder Management: Advanced skills in managing expectations and communicating design decisions to senior stakeholders across different departments.
📝 Enhancement Note: The requirements emphasize a blend of strategic thinking, hands-on design skills, and experience with enterprise-level software. The explicit mention of Figma and FigJam points to specific tool expectations. The need for experience in SaaS and cloud platforms is critical, given the role's focus on Hybrid Cloud and AI.
📊 Process & Systems Portfolio Requirements
Portfolio Essentials:
End-to-End UX Case Studies: Showcase at least 2-3 comprehensive case studies demonstrating your involvement in the entire UX lifecycle, from initial research and problem definition to final UI design and post-launch iteration for enterprise products.
Enterprise Workflow Design: Include examples that clearly illustrate your ability to design complex, multi-module user journeys and cross-surface consistency within enterprise software or SaaS platforms.
Design System Contributions: Provide evidence of your experience with design systems, whether through contributions, scaling, or maintenance, highlighting how you ensured consistency and efficiency.
Tool Proficiency Showcase: Integrate examples of your work created using Figma and FigJam, demonstrating your proficiency in creating wireframes, interactive prototypes, and high-fidelity UIs.
Problem-Solving & Impact: Clearly articulate the problems you solved, your design process, the solutions you implemented, and the measurable impact (e.g., improved user efficiency, reduced errors, enhanced adoption) of your work.
Process Documentation:
User Research & Analysis: Document your approach to user research, including methodologies used (e.g., interviews, surveys, usability testing) and how insights were synthesized to inform design decisions.
Information Architecture & Workflow Design: Detail your process for structuring complex information and designing intuitive user workflows for enterprise applications.
Design System Development & Governance: Outline your methodology for developing, documenting, and maintaining design system components and guidelines.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Illustrate your process for collaborating with Product Management, Engineering, and other stakeholders, including communication strategies and feedback integration.
📝 Enhancement Note: A strong portfolio is crucial for this role, as it directly demonstrates the candidate's ability to handle complex enterprise UX challenges. The emphasis on end-to-end case studies and design system experience is paramount.
💵 Compensation & Benefits
Salary Range: Based on industry benchmarks for Senior UX Engineers in Bucharest, Romania, with 6-10 years of experience in enterprise software/SaaS, a competitive annual salary range is estimated to be between €45,000 - €70,000 (gross) . This range accounts for the seniority of the role, the specialized skills required, and the cost of living in Bucharest.
Benefits:
Performance-Based Rewards: Performance-based salary reviews and annual bonuses to recognize and reward contributions.
Financial Incentives: Meal tickets, service anniversary awards, and referral bonuses to enhance financial well-being and employee engagement.
Ownership & Growth: Employee share purchase program and scholarships for employees’ children, fostering long-term commitment and family support.
Comprehensive Health: Fully covered private medical insurance, life & accident insurance with extra medical coverage, and an Employee Assistance Program for holistic well-being.
Wellness & Lifestyle: Annual well-being allowance for sports, training, relaxation, and therapy, plus on-site chair massage options.
Professional Development: Access to Technical Ladder & Sales Excellence programs, Individual Career Development Plans with mentoring, and a Bookster subscription for continuous learning.
Generous Time Off: 21–28 vacation days depending on tenure, sick days, extra paid leave for public holidays on weekends, and additional paid leave for employees with children.
Working Hours: This is a full-time position, typically requiring approximately 40 hours per week. The hybrid work arrangement offers flexibility in terms of location, but core working hours will likely align with standard business operations, requiring coordination with global teams.
📝 Enhancement Note: The estimated salary range is based on research for similar roles in the Romanian market, considering the specified experience level and industry. The provided benefits package is extensive and covers financial, health, professional development, and work-life balance aspects.

Industry: Technology (Hardware, Software, Services, AI, Cloud Computing)
Company Size: Large Enterprise (Lenovo is a US$83 billion revenue global technology powerhouse, serving millions of customers globally). This size implies robust processes, extensive resources, and opportunities for impact across a broad spectrum.

Data-Driven Decisions: Lenovo emphasizes data analysis and insights to drive product development and strategy.
User-Centricity: A commitment to user-centered design practices is evident in the role's description.

It sits at an individual contributor level, expected to lead complex projects and mentor junior designers. The "UX Engineer" title suggests a blend of deep UX understanding and technical design application, potentially bridging design and front-end development considerations.

Successful UX design will translate into improved customer satisfaction, increased market competitiveness, and potentially higher revenue through enhanced product adoption and retention.
